extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical researchers and academic institutions interested in Pew Scholars funding
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the Pew Scholars Program eligibility and award mechanism: grants that support independent research by early-career assistant professors working in biomedical science relevant to human health. Intended for young investigators and the academic institutions that would receive the grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target candidate: young investigators of outstanding promise
rubrics_metrics.description: The program provides funding to young investigators of outstanding promise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on individuals who demonstrate exceptional potential early in their careers; applicants should be emerging leaders in their scientific area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research focus: science relevant to the advancement of human health
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is for science relevant to the advancement of human health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research proposals should connect clearly to human health applications or implications; basic work should be framed in terms of relevance to health advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage eligibility: in first few years of appointment at assistant professor level
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants support independent research of outstanding individuals who are in their first few years of their appointment at the assistant professor level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to be early in independent academic appointments (assistant professor); senior faculty or non-academic candidates do not match this stated eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award mechanism: grants made to selected academic institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The program makes grants to selected academic institutions to support the independent research of the named individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are institutional grants intended to support the scholar's independent research program rather than direct individual fellowships; institutions are the formal grantees.
